page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.large is a general-purpose instance featuring a 2 vCPU and 8.0 GB RAM configuration, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture, the instance comprises 1 physical core running 2 threads via dedicated CPU allocation. CPU cache allocation includes 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES-NI, and VAES. The instance includes no local storage, relying on attached block storage, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation reveals strong single-core compute performance, placing in the top 25% with a stress-ng single-core score of 3070.98 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1989.0. However, multi-core scaling is constrained by the single physical core footprint, resulting in lower-tier results for stress-ng multi-core (3073.48) and Geekbench multi-core (2479.0). Memory throughput shows average performance in large block uncached writes (27.73 GB/sec), but small block cached memory bandwidth (151.05 GB/sec) and database transaction operations perform in the lower percentiles.

Given its minimal core count and entry-level resource allocation, ecs.g8a.large provides a low-cost profile suitable for utility tasks and modest workloads. Its per-core processing capability makes it efficient for single-threaded batch execution, low-concurrency application backends, and lightweight development environments. Applications with heavy concurrent thread requirements or intensive database I/O will encounter physical performance limits on this tier.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.large is a general-purpose instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at 2.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture, it incorporates 1 physical core with 2 threads on dedicated CPU allocation, supported by 32 MB L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 and VAES extensions. The instance lacks local disk storage, depending on network storage options, and maintains a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate high single-core execution speeds, ranking in the top 25%, though overall multi-threaded throughput and database transaction capacity are restricted by its single physical core constraint. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, single-threaded processing jobs, and low-traffic web applications.
